candidates.name: Hidradenocarcinoma
support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement. Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm.
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.
candidates.why: The histopathological features and immunohistochemistry results are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a rare malignant tumor of the apocrine glands.

candidates.name: Apocrine gland carcinoma
support_spans: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
Immunohistochemistry demonstrating GATA3-positive apocrine glandular structures
candidates.why: The presence of apocrine glands and the expression of GATA3 and estrogen receptor suggest a possible origin from apocrine glands.

candidates.name: Cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer
support_spans: Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
contradict_spans: Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors
candidates.why: The immunohistochemical profile and the presence of tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node could suggest a metastasis from a breast primary, although no primary tumor was detected.
